response.markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Training margins depend on score scale. Rank statistics improve comparability but remain candidate-dependent. (2) Existing probes never intervene on histories. They cannot distinguish recent-context reliance from broad association. (3) Feedback identifies redundancy and compatibility concerns. Histories do not establish ownership, fulfilled demand, or intent.

**Related work.** (1) HSTU supplies the required backbone [1]; checkpoint sensitivity requires measurement. (2) Recency research motivates temporal controls [2], while perturbation research cautions against disrupting sequential semantics [3]. (3) Sampling research distinguishes sampled discrimination from broader recommendation quality [4]; clustered inference must preserve user dependence [6].

These support three directions: sequence-sensitivity auditing, rank-based separation diagnostics, and evidence-qualified relevance auditing.

### Framework

| Direction | Observable evidence | Unresolved question |
|---|---|---|
| Separation | Target rank, negative-outranking fraction, ties | Generalization beyond sampled candidates |
| Sequence sensitivity | Paired changes under controlled interventions | Whether sensitivity reflects useful intent |
| Relevance evidence | Explicit title/description specifications | Unobserved compatibility and purchase intent |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes strengths and limitations.

1. **Matched history-intervention audit — 5/7/5.** Originality: combines useful controls, but established techniques. Potential: guides HSTU investigation, but cannot establish usefulness. Difficulty: reuses inference hooks, but alignment, timestamps, and clustering require care [1–3,6].
2. **Rank-based separation dashboard — 3/6/2.** Originality: improves scale invariance, but uses standard statistics. Potential: interpretable comparisons, but candidate-dependent. Difficulty: simple scoring, but eligibility and ties matter [4].
3. **Specification-evidence audit — 6/7/6.** Originality: separates relation, compatibility, and evidence sufficiency, but follows task definitions. Potential: explains mismatches, but incomplete descriptions limit coverage. Difficulty: feasible small audit, but credible labels require human review [5].

### Selected idea: matched history-intervention audit

At 0% progress, retain this diagnostic before changing training; the dashboard supplies its measurements. Freeze one HSTU checkpoint/category. Construct identified training prefixes with their next-item targets; exclude future positions. Compare original histories, equal-count recent/oldest deletion, final-only deletion, recent deletion preserving the final item, and repeated final-item-preserving shuffles.

Strip padding, transform, restore left padding, and read the greatest nonzero index. Freeze candidates across variants. With two candidates report pairwise accuracy, margins, and ties; HR@10 is trivial. For informative ranks, use the separately declared training-prefix candidate protocol below. These diagnostics never replace host validation HR@10.

Predeclare sampling caps, deletion size, repeats, and seeds. Cache baseline scores and bootstrap cached outcomes. Average repeats within prefixes, prefixes within users, users within categories; bootstrap user clusters and recompute macro means. Without reliable IDs, report descriptive effects only.

Preserve timestamp semantics where supported; otherwise label interventions item/position-only. Recent deletion changes the readout item, motivating final-item controls. Perturbation effects indicate sensitivity, not causal intent, useful ordering, or shortcut learning. Report coverage, ties, actual candidates, GPU time, and memory; never claim measured improvement without results.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722), [3](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-8994/17/10/1634), [4](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086), [5](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html), [6](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7148287/).

idea.description: Extend the family-aware HSTU diagnostic adapter with matched, readout-controlled history interventions and rank diagnostics using one frozen trained model per category.
idea.motivation: Existing embedding geometry and sampled training margins do not test the hypothesis that recommendations rely on broad historical associations. Paired interventions measure sensitivity without inventing intent, ownership, compatibility, or fulfilled-demand labels. Final-item controls address a key ambiguity: deleting recent events also changes the event supplying the final representation.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions through the existing schema. Preserve ModelView and view.model as the actual trained nn.Module. Use evaluation mode and torch.inference_mode(), restoring the previous training mode in finally. Retain embedding-collapse and sampled-pair metrics with explicit definitions; category breakdowns remain empty when item categories are unavailable, and raw category counts cannot support exposure-adjusted conclusions. Do not access unavailable reviews, ratings, prices, stores, or simulator traits.

Prefer constructing an audit from view.user_train['History'] with reliable user IDs. Match the corrected family-specific sample_batch next-item convention: for a loader target positive[b,t], use only sequence[b,:t+1], strip its padding, and retain positive[b,t] as the target. Never score an earlier target using later sequence positions. From public histories, equivalently use history[max(0,j-L):j] to predict history[j]. Earlier occurrences of the target remain valid context. Use the baseline's truncation length L and document truncation. Loader rows contain no user IDs; do not infer them using sequence hashes. If only loader rows are available, label results training-row diagnostics and omit user-clustered confidence intervals.

Predeclare an audit cap of 32 eligible users/category, two distinct target positions/user, and three shuffle repeats. Sort user IDs before local seed-42 sampling; choose eligible target positions deterministically using that generator. Require at least four context events for the complete matched comparison and report coverage, exclusions, unique users, and prefixes. Use k=min(3, floor((n-2)/2)). Compare recent removal h[:-k], oldest removal h[k:], final-only removal h[:-1], removal of the k events immediately preceding the final event, and permutations of h[:-1] with h[-1] fixed. Deletion variants compact surviving events before restoring left padding. This supports both final-item and equal-count deletion comparisons without leaving empty contexts.

For each prefix, freeze one target plus up to 999 unique negatives, sampled without replacement from ordinary catalog items excluding padding, reserved tokens, the target, and prefix-seen items. Never inspect later interactions or held-out labels to filter negatives. Keep the target exactly once even if previously seen. If the eligible pool is smaller, use all eligible negatives and disclose candidate counts. Use a deterministic seed derived from category index, sorted user index, and target position, not Python's randomized hash. Loader-provided single negatives support a separate pairwise diagnostic only: two-candidate HR@10 is trivially one. Label larger-candidate results training-prefix sampled diagnostics; they are distinct from the host's 200-user/category, 99-negative, seed-42 validation protocol. Define target rank by descending score, then ascending item ID, and report target tie frequency. Follow host tie rules only when reproducing its evaluator through an explicitly supplied interface; do not silently substitute this diagnostic rule.

Inspect the supplied HSTU implementation when implementing the adapter to determine whether relative-position and elapsed-time channels exist. Do not infer support from the HSTU family name. If time is consumed through an existing compatible interface, preserve surviving event timestamps and the original prediction-time reference under deletion. For shuffles, permute item identities across fixed chronological timestamp slots and label that intervention precisely. Moving item–timestamp pairs together is a distinct, potentially nonchronological intervention and is excluded from the primary protocol. An original-position-ID deletion control is optional only where already supported; never introduce padding holes as a substitute. If the model consumes only item IDs, explicitly label results item/position sensitivity and avoid elapsed-time claims. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, and predict_score(features, items); adapt tensor shapes to their actual family-specific signatures.

Extract the greatest nonpadding absolute index, never count-1. Batch and chunk candidate scoring without changing results. Cache original scores, preserve candidates across variants, and report perturbed-minus-original rank, reciprocal-rank, and hit differences with explicit sign conventions. For each intervention, average repeats within a prefix, prefixes within a user, users within each category, then take the four-category macro mean. Bootstrap 2,000 replicates with a local seed-42 generator, resampling users with replacement within categories and retaining all paired prefixes and repeats. Recompute the macro mean in each replicate and take its 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles; do not average category interval endpoints. If a verified common identity spans categories, cluster that user's complete cross-category records jointly. Do not assume matching local ID strings identify the same person. Intervals condition on the fitted checkpoints and fixed audit protocol. Without reliable IDs, provide paired descriptive effects, empirical quantiles, row counts, and seed variability only. Return null with an explicit reason for undefined statistics or missing categories rather than substituting zero or silently averaging fewer categories.

With four deterministic deletion interventions and three shuffle repeats, the declared cap is 4*32*2*(1+4+3)=2,048 sequence evaluations. Candidate scoring remains an additional cost; log actual evaluations, candidate counts, measured GPU time, and peak memory before describing the audit as inexpensive. Bootstrap cached scalar outcomes without rerunning models. Report per-category results and macro summaries; keep the protocol fixed to limit researcher selection and repeated-validation overfitting. Sensitivity can motivate hypotheses about shortcuts but cannot identify shortcut learning or establish that invariance means history is ignored.

Preserve all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches/epoch. Use local diagnostic random generators so the audit does not alter training RNG state. No architecture or prediction change is required: retain checkpoint and embedded predictor consistency, with exactly one independently trained model/category and no score fusion. Validation auditing requires host-supplied permitted contexts and candidates; do not obtain hidden labels. The fixed host macro validation HR@10 remains the selection criterion.
idea.pseudocode:
def audit_prefix(history, target, category_index, user_index, target_position, view):
    h = truncate_to_baseline_length(history)
    if len(h) < 4:
        return excluded('history_too_short')
    rng = local_rng(seed_sequence=[42, category_index, user_index, target_position])
    candidates = [target] + sample_unique_catalog_negatives(
        max_count=999, exclude=set(h) | {target, PAD} | RESERVED, rng=rng)
    k = min(3, (len(h) - 2) // 2)
    variants = {
        'original': h,
        'recent_removed': h[:-k],
        'oldest_removed': h[k:],
        'final_removed': h[:-1],
        'recent_preserving_final': concat(h[:-(k + 1)], h[-1:]),
    }
    for r in range(3):
        variants['shuffle_' + str(r)] = concat(permute(h[:-1], rng), h[-1:])
    outcomes = {}
    for name, items in variants.items():
        seq = left_pad(items, L)
        # Apply corresponding timestamp/position policy only if supported.
        feats = view.log2feats(seq[None, :])
        last = greatest_index_where(seq != PAD)
        scores = score_with_existing_predict_score_contract(
            view, feats[:, last, :], candidates)
        target_score = scores[index_of(target, candidates)]
        rank = 1 + count(scores > target_score) + count(
            (scores == target_score) & (candidate_ids < target))
        outcomes[name] = {
            'rank': rank, 'rr': 1.0 / rank, 'hit10': float(rank <= 10),
            'target_tied': any_other_candidate_equals(target_score),
            'candidate_count': len(candidates)}
    return paired_differences(outcomes, reference='original')

# Existing run_full_diagnosis retains embedding and loader-pair probes.
# Prefer identified user-history prefixes; loader fallback uses sequence[:t+1]
# and positive[t], and has descriptive reporting without user bootstrap CIs.
# Average shuffle repeats within prefixes; prefixes within users;
# users within categories; then average all four category means.
# Bootstrap complete user clusters 2,000 times and recompute macro means.
# Return metrics AND metric_definitions, with coverage and null reasons.
# Interpreter distinguishes observed sensitivity from intent and generalization.

originality.positive: Combines matched deletion, final-item controls, and dependence-aware aggregation in the HSTU diagnostic adapter.
originality.negative: The constituent interventions, rank statistics, and clustered bootstrap are established methods; this is a protocol contribution.

future_potential.positive: Can support reproducible investigation of sequence reliance and motivate subsequent single-model HSTU experiments.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix sensitivity does not establish useful intent, causal preferences, shortcut learning, or improved held-out HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses trained checkpoints and existing feature/scoring hooks without another fitted predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct prefix alignment, candidate eligibility, timestamp semantics, user identity, clustered aggregation, and cost accounting require substantial care.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU as a sequential-transduction architecture for recommendation.
limitations: Architecture-level results do not establish recent-context or order reliance for the supplied checkpoint.
The adapter must verify which temporal and positional channels the supplied implementation actually uses.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: Motivates examining excessive dependence on recent interactions.
limitations: Does not establish harmful recency bias in this benchmark's HSTU models.
Recent-event deletion requires controls for changes to the final readout item.

related_work.title: Temporal-Aware and Intent Contrastive Learning
contributions: Motivates caution when cropping, masking, or reordering sequential histories.
limitations: Perturbation effects require controls and do not directly identify user intent.

related_work.title: On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies
contributions: Distinguishes sampled discrimination from agreement with fuller evaluation and other reliability dimensions.
limitations: Does not validate these diagnostic metrics as predictors of HSTU performance on this task.
Changing diagnostic candidate counts does not change the pinned benchmark protocol.

related_work.title: TREC Product Recommendation Task Definitions
contributions: Distinguishes substitutes, complements, compatibility, and subjective preference.
limitations: Relation labels alone cannot establish redundancy, fulfilled demand, or compatibility when specifications are missing.
Evidence-qualified labels require an annotation protocol and cannot be inferred from interaction co-occurrence alone.

related_work.title: Cluster-bootstrap methodology
contributions: Supports preserving within-subject dependence through cluster-level resampling.
limitations: Requires reliable cluster identities and a resampling scheme aligned with the estimand.
Does not remove training-set optimism or account for uncertainty across independently trained checkpoints.

related_work.title: SASRec reference sampler
contributions: Illustrates shifted next-item sequence and target alignment.
limitations: Serves only as an alignment reference; the supplied HSTU sampler remains authoritative.
Does not justify changing the required HSTU backbone.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows why sampled-candidate metrics require care when comparing recommendation models.
limitations: Does not make larger-candidate training diagnostics equivalent to full-catalog or held-out evaluation.

related_work.title: SciPy rankdata documentation
contributions: Documents differing conventions for assigning ranks to tied values.
limitations: The proposed item-ID tie rule must be implemented explicitly; it is not implied by a generic ranking function.

related_work.title: Scikit-learn permutation importance documentation
contributions: Illustrates explicit sampling and repeat controls for perturbation-based measurements.
limitations: Generic feature permutation does not establish the validity of sequential-history interventions or population confidence intervals.

related_work.title: Additional HSTU analysis supplied in the search results
contributions: Motivates checking relative-position and elapsed-time attention channels.
limitations: The supplied corrected baseline may implement only a subset of these channels.

related_work.title: CETD temporal counterfactual research
contributions: Motivates preserving temporal dependencies and proximity to observed histories when interpreting interventions.
limitations: Does not turn deletion or shuffle diagnostics into causal evidence about user preferences.
